result.topic_en: Dated 18 January 1797, the page multiplies the integrals of x dx/(1-x^3)^{1/3} and dx/(1-x^3)^{2/3} as power series, expands infinite products into series, and records a note on Laplace's theorem about particular solutions and integrating factors of differential equations.

Expression of the product of integrals with integration constants C, C'

Laplace's theorem relating particular solutions of dy=p dx to a common divisor of two expressions

items.quote:
La Place demonstrait
Si $\mu=0$ sit solutio particularis aeq.
$dy=pdx$ tum fore $\mu$ divisorem communem quantitatum
items.english: Laplace proved: if μ=0 is a particular solution of the equation dy=p dx, then μ is a common divisor of the quantities p+(d²p/dxdy)/(d²p/dy²) and 1/(dp/dy).
